newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare losses on bottom-fishing.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare losses on bottom-fishing.

text.p: Mexican stocks were down but had cut earlier losses at midday dealing on Friday after bargain-hunters had tentatively stepped into the market, traders said.
"Prices began to look attractive again below the 5,000-point mark, and buyers stepped in. We don't have as many foreign investors as yesterday, but they are here," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was down 29.27 points, or 0.58 percent, at 5,038.56.

Dealers said the recovery was most notable in market heavyweights Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) and Bancomer, which accounted for more than 40 percent of all shares traded, not including one hefty cross trade.
Telecomms firm Telmex L shares had pared its earlier slide of 25 centavos to 5 centavos and were trading at 21.55 pesos.
Financial firm Bancomer was down 12 centavos to 5.66 pesos, but off an earlier low of 5.48 pesos.
On the broad market, sliders outpaced gainers by 55 to 28.
